Kidderminster Crufts star returns to competitive grooming

4 hrs ago
Pets
By Matthew O’Hara Senior Reporter

Share

0 comments
Read More

lorry overturns
Mia and Scrabby (Image: Supplied)

Instaread

A teenage Crufts winner from Kidderminster has celebrated finishing second in her first grooming competition in four months.

Mia Blackburn, alongside her beloved cockerpoo, Scrabby, scooped second place in the 'Intermediate Group 2' category at 'I'm a Groomer Get Me Out of Hair', which was held at Fen Drayton Village Hall in Cambridge on Saturday (October 3).

The latest award for Mia is her fifth with Scrabby, with her haul also including first place in the Crufts 2026 dog grooming competition.

The competition was also Mia's first since June, as she focused on opening her brand new grooming salon 'Mia Pretty Paws', which is based in Renfrew Gardens in Kidderminster.

For Mia, the break from competing meant that she could enjoy her return to competitive grooming.

She said: “I think this competition was the most fun I have ever had at one before.

“My mind and all of my energy have been so focused on the new business that I hadn’t prepared for it nearly as much as I would’ve previously.

“So to walk into it with no nerves, or any pressure, I had the best time and just enjoyed grooming Scrabby and connecting with others.

“So I went on Saturday not expecting anything to come from it, and to still walk away with second place in what I felt was a really tough class with so much talent surrounding me, is really special, and I feel really proud.

“Me and Scrabby now have five awards together. He truly is my lucky charm, and I’m lucky to have met a dog like him.

“I’ll always be grateful to his parents for allowing me to use him like my own.”

As well as her second-place finish at 'I'm a Groomer Get Me Out of Hair', Mia was also 'honoured' to be a finalist for ‘best beginner competition groomer’ at the event.

Mia and Scrabby are now preparing for their next competitive outing at 'Groomphoria' in Coventry next month.
